title: Fasten a strut fitting at a mark with a spring nut: edge-on into the slot, quarter turn under the lips, bolt hand-snug
instruction: Fasten the square plate fitting to the strut at the red mark with its spring nut and bolt. Leave the bolt hand-snug, not torqued. Do not drop any of the parts, and let go of them when you are done.
context: Fastening fittings to strut channel (Unistrut and similar) with spring nuts is everyday work for electricians (SOC 47-2111, about 821,000 jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook), plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (47-2152, about 510,600) and HVAC mechanics (49-9021, about 440,900): racks, supports and trapezes for conduit, pipe, boxes and equipment are built from it. The usual way (not given to the robot): push the nut edge-on through the slot, past the lips against its spring, turn it a quarter turn clockwise so its grooves catch the lips, slide it to the mark, run the bolt down hand-snug. Fittings are set this way, checked, then torqued with a wrench (50 ft-lb for 1/2 in); this task ends at hand-snug, ready for the torque wrench, and does not scale the torque down.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Channel: a 61 cm (2 ft) length of Unistrut P1000 strut (1-5/8 x 1-5/8 in, 12 ga, green Perma-Green finish; 7/8 in slot, lips turned in and down 9/32 in) bolted flat to the table, open side up, running left-right from 30.5 cm right to 30.5 cm left of the midline, its axis 30.0 cm in front of the bases, top 4.1 cm up; 3/8 in anchor bolts with square washers through its back at 13 and 25 cm either side of the midline. Mark: red tape 12 mm wide across the channel's near wall and near lip, centred 4.0 cm right of the midline. Kit, on a wooden block (6 x 6 cm, 6.6 cm tall, with a 2.4 x 3.8 cm pocket) centred 21.5 cm in front of the bases and 17.0 cm right of the midline: a zinc Unistrut P1064 square plate fitting (1-5/8 in square, 1/4 in thick, 9/16 in hole) flat on the block, edges square to the channel; through it a 1/2-13 x 15/16 in hex head cap screw (3/4 in across flats), head down on the fitting, two flats facing left and right; on it, started two turns, a Unistrut P1010 1/2-13 spring nut (19 x 34.5 x 12.7 mm, coil spring below) hanging in the pocket, its long side left-right.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial, from the moment it happens, whatever was reached before or after: the kit dropped (the fitting, the nut or the bolt on the table, off the channel and off the block), or the nut run off the bolt (engaged less than half a turn; it falls into the channel). Otherwise the highest level reached: 0.25 the spring nut seated under the lips (turned across the channel within 10 degrees, both grooves on the lips: its top within 1.2 mm of the seated height, centred within 3 mm); 0.5 also the bolt's centre within 3 mm of the mark's centre line along the channel; 0.75 also the bolt engaged 5 turns or more; 1.0 the after-release check passed. It starts once every fingertip has stayed at least 3 cm from the fitting and the bolt for 1 s without a break (the count restarts if one comes closer); the 0.75 conditions, the fitting flat on the lips (gap under 0.6 mm, tilt under 2 degrees), square to the channel within 3 degrees and the head down on it (gap under 0.5 mm) must hold; then pull the fitting along the channel with 20 N for 2 s: pass if it moves less than 1 mm (hand-snug, not torqued). Checked with a rule from the tape's centre to the bolt, turns counted on the video, feeler gauge, square and a spring scale.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo finishes in 2,308 steps (115 s)
reset_notes: Back the bolt out to two turns engaged, push the nut down and turn it a quarter turn anticlockwise inside the channel, lift the kit out by the bolt's head and stand it back in the block's pocket (nut long side left-right, fitting square, two head flats facing left and right). Check the red tape. About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX 480 Hz, i2rt arm gains. P1000 lips and P1010 nut modelled from catalog dimensions: nut passes the slot only edge-on, turns only clockwise inside, stops at a quarter turn; grooves catch the lips. Spring a sprung joint (440 N/m, inferred). Thread a screw rule (1.954 mm/turn, friction T = 0.03 + 0.2 d F N m); no cross-threading. Pull check applied in sim. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reaches toward the kit, never lifts it); demo (cameras and joint states only): 1.0; control (no quarter turn, forced pull check): 0.0
